roles.summary: Employers screen research scientists mainly on credentials: PhD plus first-author papers at NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR, with hands-on LLM / generative-model work as the dominant topic. US and EU (London) frontier labs and startups want PhD and publications; India roles (Wipro, Microsoft Bengaluru) are similar at senior level but accept a Master's plus ability to reproduce papers at entry level. Specific theory topics in the path (learning theory, SSMs, JEPA) are almost never named.

roles.summary: Research engineers are hired on hands-on large-scale training: PyTorch/JAX, multi-node distributed training (FSDP, ZeRO, DeepSpeed, Megatron), parallelism strategies and GPU efficiency. US and EU postings focus on pretraining infrastructure and scale (hundreds to thousands of GPUs, SLURM/K8s), while India postings lean toward post-training open 7B+ models (SFT, DPO/RLHF with TRL/OpenRLHF), ablations and Indic-language data. The path's core matches well; optimizer and init frontier topics are rarely asked.

roles.summary: In 2026 'AI for science' hiring is overwhelmingly drug discovery and protein design: employers want a PhD (or MS + experience), molecular generative models (diffusion/flow matching), geometric deep learning and real biological/chemical data experience. US startups emphasise generative protein design with wet-lab loops; London adds top-venue publications and 3D/geometric DL; India demand sits in Hyderabad pharma centres (Novartis) at senior levels with production/lifecycle skills. Physics/weather topics were not asked.

The map's biggest hole is infrastructure: no topic covers containers, Kubernetes, cloud or monitoring.

The path's serving topics fit, but kernel programming and profiling have no dedicated topic.

US roles pay most and add synthetic data and contamination analysis; London/Berlin emphasise data-platform tools; India is dominated by services-firm GenAI/RAG pipelines. The path fits the curation side well but misses the platform tooling and RAG ingestion side.

roles.summary: Safety employers want demonstrated alignment research (papers, MATS-style fellowships, open-source), hands-on interpretability and post-training (SFT/RLHF), plus strong Python/PyTorch engineering. US labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Scale) pay $216k-$690k and accept non-PhDs with strong output, sometimes asking for governance frameworks; London (AISI, DeepMind) emphasises interpretability, red-teaming, oversight and agent control; Bengaluru roles centre on RLHF/reward modeling and jailbreak robustness, with research tracks expecting a PhD. The path's targets match well; it under-weights hands-on training and evals.
